quotes: In March 2026, Provisional Measure No. 1,340 introduced the Export Tax (IE) on exports of crude petroleum oils or oils obtained from bituminous minerals, as well as road diesel fuel, effective as of March 12, 2026.
Following the expiration ofthe provisional measure on July 9, 2026, the taxation of crude oil exports was maintained through Gecex Resolutions Nos. 938, 957 and 977/2026 until December 31, 2026.
Through September 2026, Petrobras' Export Tax payments totaled R$ 6.9 billion.

material_events.basis: Stated in the Form 6-K dated November 16, 2026.
material_events.claim: Petrobras announced the upcoming Board of Directors approval submission and investor webcast for its new 2027-2031 Business Plan.
quotes: Rio de Janeiro, November 16, 2026 –Petróleo Brasileiro S.A. – Petrobras informs that on November 24, 2026, it will hold a webcast featuring the Company's Executive Board to present the new 2027-2031 Business Plan (2027-31 BP), which will be submitted to its Board of Directors for approval on November 23, 2026.

material_events.basis: Stated in the Form 6-K dated November 16, 2026.
material_events.claim: Petrobras received new installments under the diesel Economic Subvention Programs, bringing cumulative receipts under the diesel, gasoline, and LPG subsidy programs to approximately R$ 18 billion.
quotes: With these payments, the cumulative amount received by Petrobras under the diesel, gasoline, and LPG subsidy programs totals approximately R$ 18 billion.

material_events.basis: Stated in the 3Q26 Form 6-K financial performance release (effective 2026-11-13T14:30:00Z).
material_events.claim: Petrobras raised its 2026 average production estimate from guidance of 3.1 million barrels of oil equivalent per day to between 3.3 and 3.4 million barrels per day.
quotes: Our production guidance pointed to an average of 3.1 million barrels of oil equivalent per day in 2026, but we currently estimate an average between 3.3 and 3.4 million barrels per day.

quotes: We have revised our total Capex guidance (Portfolio Under Implementation) for 2026 from US$ 19.4 billion (+/- 5%) to a range of US$ 24 billion to US$ 25.5 billion, while our cash Capex guidance (Portfolio Under Implementation) was revised from US$ 16.9 billion (+/- 5%) to a range of US$ 21 billion to US$ 22 billion.

risks.basis: Stated in P2 (Export Tax introduction, rates, R$ 6.9 billion payment, and 35% federal tax increase); cash-flow pressure risk inferred from cash tax outflows and countered by production-driven cash flow guidance stated in P6.
risks.claim: Petrobras paid R$ 6.9 billion in Export Tax under a 12% general rate and a 6% EU rate, driving a 35% increase in federal tax payments.
quotes: In March 2026, Provisional Measure No. 1,340 introduced the Export Tax (IE) on exports of crude petroleum oils or oils obtained from bituminous minerals, as well as road diesel fuel, effective as of March 12, 2026.
Following the expiration ofthe provisional measure on July 9, 2026, the taxation of crude oil exports was maintained through Gecex Resolutions Nos. 938, 957 and 977/2026 until December 31, 2026.

The Export Tax on crude oil is generally levied at a 12% rate and at a 6% rate on exports to the European Union, pursuant to the Interim Trade Agreement between the European Union (EU) and the Southern Common Market (Mercosur).
Through September 2026, Petrobras' Export Tax payments totaled R$ 6.9 billion.
Compared with the same period of 2025, federal tax payments increased by 35%, mainly due to the higher corporate income tax collections and the introduction of the Export Tax.
